notes.sowing: Sow thinly {cm:1} deep from 4 weeks before your last frost, in rows {cm:20} apart, and sow a short row every 2 weeks for a steady supply. Hardy types sown in late summer stand the winter for an early spring crop.
notes.care: Thin to about {cm:2.5} apart, as crowding invites downy mildew. Keep weeded and watered, since the thin leaves cannot shade out weeds. Bunching onions can be left as a clump and divided.
notes.harvest: Pull when about {cm:15} tall, around 2 months after sowing, or cut the leaves and let them regrow several times. Older plants have a stronger flavor.
